description:
pkix-path/src/lib.rs:1109-1116 — prune_policy_tree removes ancestor nodes that have no children, but the matching logic is:
  `child_policies.iter().any(|cp| n.expected_policy_set.contains(cp))`

This checks whether any child's valid_policy appears in the PARENT's expected_policy_set. This is intentional: after policy mappings, the parent's expected_policy_set contains the OIDs that were expected to appear as children's valid_policies. If a child's valid_policy appears in the parent's expected_policy_set, the parent has a child.

However, RFC 5280 §6.1.3(d)(3) says to prune nodes that have no child nodes — meaning nodes in the TREE (no descendant node at depth i). The code checks expected_policy_set match which is semantic rather than structural. For the case where expected_policy_set was updated by PolicyMappings, a parent node may expect OID X but the cert asserted OID Y (mapped from X). In this case the child's valid_policy would be Y, but the parent's expected_policy_set was updated to contain Y by the mapping step. So this is correct.

BUT: after policy mappings set expected_policy_set to [sdp] (line 2343), the prune check looks for child_policies.contains(sdp). Children are created with valid_policy = cert's policy OID. If the cert asserted sdp then the match works. If it didn't, the node should be pruned. This appears correct.

Not a bug on further analysis.
title: prune_policy_tree: incorrect parent-child matching uses valid_policy instead of expected_policy_set
